CVE-2025-15224 is the libssh key passphrase bypass: during SCP/SFTP public key authentication curl could wrongly fall back to authenticating via a locally running SSH agent. The upstream advisory (curl.se/docs/CVE-2025-15224.html) states the flaw 'only exists when libcurl is built to use the libssh backend, not the libssh2 based one'. Verified in the built image: `curl --version` reports libssh2/1.11.1 as the SSH backend, the installed libcurl is the OpenSSL/libssh2 flavour (libcurl4t64 8.14.1-2+deb13u3), and no libssh library exists on the filesystem. The vulnerable libssh agent-fallback code is not compiled in.

CVE-2025-15079 is the libssh global known_hosts override: during SCP/SFTP transfers libcurl could accept hosts absent from the caller-specified known_hosts file if the libssh built-in global known_hosts recognized them. The upstream advisory (curl.se/docs/CVE-2025-15079.html) states the flaw 'only exists when libcurl is built to use the libssh backend, not the libssh2 based one'. Verified in the built image: `curl --version` reports libssh2/1.11.1 as the SSH backend, the installed libcurl is the OpenSSL/libssh2 flavour (libcurl4t64 8.14.1-2+deb13u3), and no libssh library exists on the filesystem. The vulnerable libssh known_hosts fallback code is not compiled in.

CVE-2025-14017 is an unsynchronized-shared-data flaw where multi-threaded LDAPS transfers through libcurl let TLS options set in one thread leak into concurrent transfers in other threads. The upstream advisory (curl.se/docs/CVE-2025-14017.html) scopes the flaw to libcurl only ('affects: lib'); the curl command line tool is not affected because it does not run concurrent transfers across threads. Verified in the built image: an ldd scan of every executable under /bin, /sbin, /usr/bin, /usr/sbin and /usr/local/bin shows /usr/bin/curl is the only binary linking libcurl, no libcurl development headers are present (libcurl4t64 only, /usr/include/curl does not exist), dockerize is a statically linked Go binary, and the JVM does not use libcurl. No multi-threaded libcurl consumer exists in the image, so the racy threaded-LDAPS code path cannot be executed.

CVE-2025-10966 is a missing SFTP host-verification flaw in curl's wolfSSH-powered SSH backend. Debian does not build curl against wolfSSH: verified in the built image, `curl --version` reports libssh2/1.11.1 as the SSH backend (full line: curl 8.14.1 ... libssh2/1.11.1 ... OpenLDAP/2.6.10), the installed packages are curl and libcurl4t64 8.14.1-2+deb13u3 (OpenSSL flavour), and no wolfSSH or wolfSSL library exists on the filesystem. The vulnerable wolfSSH connection-management code is not compiled in.

CVE-2025-15224 makes curl wrongly authenticate via a locally running SSH agent when asked to do public key authentication for SCP/SFTP transfers. No component in this image performs scp:// or sftp:// transfers via libcurl: there is no curl CLI, no SSH agent runs in the container, and the only two libcurl consumers found by a DT_NEEDED scan of every ELF object (librdkafka.so.1 and the IBM DB2 clidriver GSKit library) contain zero scp or sftp scheme strings and drive HTTPS only. The vulnerable SSH authentication path is never entered. No fixed version exists for trixie.

CVE-2025-15079 makes libcurl accept SSH hosts from the SSH library's global known_hosts file even when a transfer-specific known_hosts file is set, during SCP/SFTP transfers. No component in this image performs scp:// or sftp:// transfers via libcurl: the image has no curl CLI, and the only two libcurl consumers found by a DT_NEEDED scan of every ELF object (librdkafka.so.1 and the IBM DB2 clidriver GSKit library) contain zero scp or sftp scheme strings and drive HTTPS only. The vulnerable SSH transfer setup is therefore never entered; the advisory also describes the libssh global known_hosts behavior while Debian builds libcurl against libssh2. No fixed version exists for trixie.

CVE-2025-14017 leaks TLS option changes between concurrent multi-threaded LDAPS transfers in libcurl. The image ships no curl CLI (only libcurl4t64 as a library dependency), and a DT_NEEDED scan of every ELF object in the built image finds exactly two libcurl consumers: librdkafka.so.1 (uses libcurl solely for HTTPS OIDC token retrieval; the binary contains zero ldap scheme strings) and the IBM DB2 clidriver GSKit library bundled in site-packages (certificate and revocation handling). Neither performs LDAPS transfers through libcurl, let alone the vulnerable pattern of concurrent multi-threaded LDAPS transfers that mutate per-transfer TLS options; datahub's LDAP ingestion source uses the pure-Python python-ldap stack via libldap2, which does not route through libcurl. No fixed version exists for trixie.

CVE-2025-10966 is a missing host-verification flaw in curl's wolfSSH-powered SFTP backend. Debian does not build curl against wolfSSH: verified in the built image that libcurl.so.4.8.0 contains zero wolfssh references while libssh2 references are present (the SSH backend is libssh2), so the vulnerable wolfSSH code is not compiled into the shipped library. This matches the central Debian assessment that the wolfSSH code is not used in Debian.

The DHI curl package backports the upstream libssh public key auth fix from https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/16d5f2a5660c61cc27bd5f1c7f512391d1c927aa as dhi-cve-2025-15224-libssh-publickey-auth.patch.
The DHI curl package backports the upstream libssh known_hosts fix from https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/adca486c125d9a6d9565b9607a19dce803a8b479 as dhi-cve-2025-15079-libssh-knownhosts.patch.

The DHI curl package backports the upstream LDAP per-connection option fix from https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/39d1976b7f709a516e3243338ebc0443bdd8d56d as dhi-cve-2025-14017-ldap-per-connection-options.patch.
The vulnerable wolfSSH backend is not built in the DHI curl package.
